evidence.finding: Output encoding: FastAPI/ORJSON auto-escapes to prevent XSS. HTML content in JSON responses is safely encoded. No raw HTML output from backend API (JSON-only API).
Content-Type header charset encoding: application/json; charset=utf-8 for API responses. utf-8 encoding throughout.
HTML output encoding: ORJSON and Pydantic ensure JSON-safe escaping. Any HTML content in API responses is JSON-encoded (escaped). Frontend React handles rendering.
Unicode encoding: Python/JSON handles unicode escaping. No mixed or malicious encoding vectors.
Database query encoding: SQLAlchemy ORM with parameterized queries. SQL injection prevented by ORM query builder and raw SQL with text() bind parameters.

SSRF protection: External URL fetching via httpx with timeout. URL allowlist not explicitly coded but external service requests are hardcoded to known endpoints (OpenBao, Keycloak, Redis). No user-controlled URL fetch paths.
Safe JSON deserialization: Pydantic models validate structure and types. No eval-based deserialization. Schema validation prevents unsafe data structures.

evidence.source: No eval() or exec() found (rg eval/exec patterns returns 0 hits for dangerous usage)
evidence.finding: No eval() or exec() with user input. Template rendering is server-side React (Next.js) or Pydantic serialization. No SSTI vectors.
No Angular/Vue-style data binding framework. React with unidirectional data flow.
Unicode homoglyph attack prevention not explicitly verified. Keycloak handles username normalization. Password verification is exact-match.
Email sender uses a template-based system. User input passed as template context variables, not as raw SMTP commands. SMTP/IMAP injection prevented by email library (smtplib).
Python manages memory automatically (garbage collection). No unsafe memory operations, pointers, or buffer overflows possible in CPython. Native C extensions not used for user input processing.
Python integers are arbitrary precision - no integer overflow possible. No C/C++ code in the stack that would be vulnerable to integer overflow.
Python garbage collector handles memory deallocation. No dangling pointers or use-after-free possible in CPython.
No XML parser (lxml, ElementTree, SAX, DOM) used in the stack. rg returns 0 hits for XML parsing patterns.
Deserialization uses Pydantic models with strict field validation. extra='forbid' rejects unknown fields. No pickle, yaml.load, or other unsafe deserialization used.

Input validation rules documented via Pydantic schemas. Every write endpoint has a Pydantic BaseModel with field constraints (min_length, max_length, regex patterns, etc.). Validation rules are self-documenting via type annotations.

Logical consistency of combined data enforced via Pydantic validators. Cross-field validation in model validators (e.g., @model_validator for date ranges). Business rule validation in service layer (src/backend/services/).

Business logic limits and validations documented in system-wiki. Rate limits: 3 layers (nginx, Redis, Keycloak). Per-user limits: incident create/edit/validate quotas. Global limits: max attachments 50MB.
All write endpoints use Pydantic models for input validation. 15+ schema files in src/backend/schemas/. Field types, constraints, and validation rules defined in schemas.
Structured data validation at trusted service (backend). FastAPI auto-validates request bodies against Pydantic schemas. Trusted service boundary: nginx -> FastAPI -> validation -> service.
Combination/range rules enforced via Pydantic @model_validator decorators. Cross-field validation for incident data (e.g., date ranges, location coordinates within region constraints).

Sequential step enforcement in incident workflow: encoder creates -> drafts -> validator validates -> analyst reviews. State machine transitions enforced in business logic layer. Incident status transitions validated by role context.
Business logic limits enforced: max incidents per batch, max draft age, rate limits per user/role. Anti-automation via nginx rate limiter + Redis sliding window + Keycloak brute force (3 layers).
Business logic transactions: SQLAlchemy session with commit/rollback pattern. Service layer functions are atomic - succeed entirely or rollback. DB constraints + RLS enforce consistency.

No double-booking scenario (WIMS-BFP does not manage limited quantity resources like seats/slots). Incident data uses draft/validate workflow with status transitions. RLS prevents concurrent modification conflicts.

Three-layer anti-automation: (1) nginx limit_req zones (public_api: 10r/s, civilian_api: 5r/s, general_api: 30r/s, keycloak_api: 10r/s). (2) Backend Redis sliding-window rate limiter (utils/rate_limit.py). (3) Keycloak bruteForceProtected: true, failureFactor: 5.
Logout functionality clearly visible: signOut button in Header component. POST /api/auth/logout to revoke server-side session, then Keycloak signoutRedirect.
React uses createTextNode internally when rendering text content in JSX. No dangerous dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage (0 hits on rg).
Cookie attribute Secure: Set-Cookie with secure:true on all auth cookies. Production TLS ensures cookie transmitted over HTTPS only.
SameSite=Strict on all auth cookies. Prevents CSRF on auth-related endpoints. '__Host-' prefix used (__Host-access_token, __Host-refresh_token).
__Host- prefix used on all auth cookies (__Host-access_token, __Host-refresh_token). Path=/. Ensures cookie is scoped to the origin and cannot be set by subdomain.
Auth cookies set with HttpOnly: true. Session tokens (access_token, refresh_token) only transferred via Set-Cookie header, never accessible to JavaScript (HttpOnly).
HSTS: max-age=31536000 (1 year); includeSubDomains. Exceeds ASVS minimum of 31536000 seconds.
Cache-Control for sensitive responses: proxy_cache off for SSE endpoints. Cookie-based auth tokens are not cached by nginx (no proxy_cache directive on auth routes).

CSP header configured: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; img-src 'self' data: https://*.tile.openstreetmap.org https://unpkg.com; connect-src 'self' https://*.tile.openstreetmap.org https://wimsbfp.tech; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; worker-src 'self' https://www.gstatic.com; frame-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'. Note: 'unsafe-inline' for scripts is required for Next.js hydration.
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Set in production nginx HTTPS block. Prevents MIME-type sniffing.
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin. Configured in production nginx HTTPS block.
frame-ancestors 'self' included in CSP header. Prevents clickjacking. X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN also set as fallback.

OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) enforced by oidc-client-ts. The response_type parameter is set to 'code' (authorization code flow). Implicit flow disabled (implicitFlowEnabled: false in realm clients).

CORS preflight enforced for sensitive endpoints. Non-safelisted methods (PUT, DELETE, PATCH) trigger preflight. Production CORS uses $cors_origin map (whitelist). Content-Type validation: application/json triggers preflight.
Sensitive endpoints use POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE methods only. GET requests do not modify state. FastAPI auto-rejects unsafe methods with 405.

evidence.source: NGINX same-origin: all services on same hostname
evidence.finding: In production, all services served under wimsbfp.tech or wims.bfp.gov.ph. Same-origin policy provides natural isolation. No cross-origin apps hosted.

evidence.source: No postMessage usage in WIMS-BFP frontend
evidence.finding: rg returns 0 hits for postMessage, addEventListener('message'), or onmessage in frontend code.
No deprecated plugins: no Flash, ActiveX, Silverlight, Java applets, NACL, NSAPI. Modern client-side: React/Next.js. No browser plugins required.
Redirect destination controlled: Keycloak redirectUris allowlist on oidc client. Nginx does not follow user-controlled redirects. Logout redirect to configured post_logout_redirect_uri only.
Restrictive HTTP method allowlist per endpoint. FastAPI automatically rejects methods not defined on a route. HEAD and OPTIONS handled automatically. 405 Method Not Allowed for undefined methods.
HTTPS enforced on all user-facing endpoints via nginx TLS termination. HSTS header ensures HTTPS-only. HTTP -> HTTPS redirect for wimsbfp.tech.

No client-overridable headers (X-Forwarded-For overridden by nginx proxy_set_header in every location block). X-Real-IP uses $realip_remote_addr which is the TCP socket address. X-Forwarded-For set to $remote_addr (nginx-calculated). Verified by test_nginx_forwarded_headers.py.
HTTP request smuggling prevented by nginx normalization + FastAPI HTTP parser. nginx rejects malformed Transfer-Encoding headers. Suricata IDS monitors for smuggling patterns.
No GraphQL endpoint or library in WIMS-BFP. REST API only.
GraphQL not used.
WIMS-BFP uses SSE (Server-Sent Events) for real-time events, not WebSocket. SSE streams over HTTPS. No ws:// or wss:// connections.
WebSocket not used.
WebSocket not used.
WebSocket not used.
File handling documented in security-baseline.md S_GitLab GH #150 gaps section. Upload limits (50 MB), extension validation, storage isolation documented.
client_max_body_size 50M configured in nginx. Also enforced at backend via upload_validation.py.
File extension allowlist: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .pdf, .doc, .docx. Magic byte verification for MIME type validation. Content-Type header also verified server-side.
Filename sanitization applied - user-supplied filenames are not used directly in filesystem paths. Safe random UUID-based filenames assigned server-side.

Uploaded files stored in Docker volume incident_attachments_data mounted at /app/storage. NOT webroot. Non-executable path prevents code execution. Known gap: filesystem storage is unencrypted (GH #151).
File paths constructed server-side using UUIDs, not user-supplied names. No path traversal risk in file storage.
Downloaded files use server-generated UUID filenames. Content-Disposition header set by nginx/backend with sanitized filename. User-submitted filenames validated and not used directly.
Filenames encoded/sanitized: UUID-based filenames prevent injection via filename. Original filename stored in database, not used in filesystem paths. RFC 6266 compliance not explicitly verified.
No antivirus scanning for downloaded files. Same gap as V5.3.3 - no AV scanning at all. Risk: LOW for prototype.

bruteForceProtected: true, failureFactor: 5, maxFailureWaitSeconds: 900, waitIncrementSeconds: 300. Rate limiting also at nginx (limit_req) and backend utils/rate_limit.py. Documented in overrides File § V6.

No documented list of context-specific words found. Should include permutations of organization name (BFP), product name (WIMS), project codenames, department/role names (ENCODER, VALIDATOR, ANALYST, ADMIN), and related terms.

Single authentication pathway: Keycloak OIDC (realm=bfp, client=wims-web). Only one IdP. Direct Grant flow for password verification, authorization code flow (PKCE) for browser login. Custom email change flow documented as secondary mechanism. Documented in security-baseline.md.
passwordPolicy: length(12) and upperCase(1) and lowerCase(1) and digits(1) and specialChars(1). Minimum 12 chars exceeds ASVS L2 requirement of >= 8.
resetPasswordAllowed: true. Keycloak self-service password change via Direct Grant. UPDATE_PASSWORD required action for new users.
change_email endpoint requires current_password validated against Keycloak via Direct Grant token exchange (routes/auth.py:86-108). Password change via Keycloak requires current password.
No HIBP or top-3000-passwords SPI deployed. Documented gap (overrides V6.2.4 exception). Remediation: Keycloak password policy SPI or HIBP API integration.

passwordPolicy requires upperCase(1), lowerCase(1), digits(1), specialChars(1). ASVS 5.0 V6.2.5 states no requirement for minimum character types. Three-layer defense may justify; recommend documented rationale or removal.
Password input handled by Keycloak redirect-based OIDC flow using type=password. No WIMS frontend code renders a password field.
No paste-blocking JavaScript. Keycloak default login permits paste, browser password helpers, and managers.
Backend receives password as-is via ChangeEmailRequest.current_password (str). No truncation or transformation. Keycloak Direct Grant receives password verbatim.
Keycloak supports passwords up to 256 chars. No truncation in WIMS backend or frontend layers.
No periodic password rotation policy. ASVS 5.0 requires passwords stay valid until compromised or user-rotated. Compliant by absence of rotation policy.
No context-specific word list documented. Should include BFP, WIMS, fire, Philippines regions, role names (ENCODER, VALIDATOR, etc.).
No breached password check (HIBP or similar). Documented gap (overrides exception). Remediation: Keycloak HIBP SPI or custom endpoint.

Three-layer defense: (1) Keycloak bruteForceProtected: true, failureFactor: 5, maxFailureWaitSeconds: 900, waitIncrementSeconds: 300, permanentLockout: false, quickLoginCheckMilliSeconds: 1000. (2) nginx limit_req zones. (3) Backend Redis sliding-window rate limiter (utils/rate_limit.py).

No default accounts found in Keycloak realm users. registrationAllowed: false prevents self-registration. Default admin (Keycloak master admin) uses credentials from .env, not hardcoded. UPDATE_PASSWORD required action on new users ensures temporary passwords are changed.

SKIP_MFA realm role exists and exempts test users (validator_test, n-val, g-val, e-val, r-val) from TOTP/OTP requirement. TOTP is configured and enabled (CONFIGURE_TOTP required action enabled, defaultAction: true) but SKIP_MFA bypasses it. Documented exception per system-wiki/security/security-baseline.md S_SKIP_MFA RoleS. Must be removed before production per docs/agents/remove-demo-otp-bypass.md. Remediation: Remove SKIP_MFA role and all user assignments before production deployment. Risk: HIGH.

Single authentication pathway: Keycloak OIDC authorization code flow for browser, Direct Grant for server-side password verification (email change). No undocumented pathways. Security controls (token validation, JWKS verification, audience/issuer validation, revocation check) enforced consistently across all paths.

System-generated temporary passwords (create_keycloak_user) use secrets.choice with 14-char length, PWD_ALPHABET (upper+lower+digits+special). Passwords expire: UPDATE_PASSWORD required action set on creation forces change on first login. Temporary passwords do not become long-term passwords.
No password hints or knowledge-based authentication (secret questions) present in the application. Keycloak does not have secret question functionality enabled.

Forgot password flow uses Keycloak resetCredentialsFlow. TOTP is not bypassed during password reset (CONFIGURE_TOTP is a separate required action). The reset flow sends an email with a reset link (actionTokenGeneratedByUserLifespan: 300s = 5 min).

evidence.source: No MFA factor recovery scenario in current stack
evidence.finding: WIMS-BFP does not implement physical or hardware MFA token enrollment/issuance. TOTP is self-service via Keycloak. Factor recovery for lost TOTP device would go through Keycloak admin recovery (identity proofing at admin discretion). No automated recovery process that would bypass identity proofing.
Keycloak TOTP single-use enforced by default. otpPolicyCodeReusable is false. Each TOTP code can only be used once (look-ahead window of 1 for clock skew tolerance).
Keycloak hashes TOTP seeds using PBKDF2 with random salt before storage. TOTP seeds stored securely within Keycloak's database, not exposed to WIMS backend.
Keycloak uses SecureRandom (CSPRNG) for all TOTP seed generation. WIMS backend uses secrets.choice and secrets.randbelow for verification codes (routes/auth.py:70) and temp passwords.
Email verification codes are 6-digit (20 bits of entropy: 10^6 = ~20 bits), meeting the minimum 20-bit requirement. Generated via secrets.randbelow using CSPRNG.
TOTP lifetime: 30 seconds (otpPolicyPeriod: 30). Out-of-band (email verification code) lifetime: 10 minutes (600 seconds). Both within ASVS limits (30s for TOTP, 10 min for OOB).

evidence.source: WIMS-BFP does not use PSTN/SMS OTP
evidence.finding: No PSTN, phone, or SMS OTP delivery in the WIMS-BFP stack. The only MFA mechanism is TOTP via Keycloak. No phone number validation scenario exists for auth.
WIMS-BFP does not implement OOB authentication requests. TOTP is the only second factor, and it uses shared-secret-based time-synchronized codes (in-band).
No code-based OOB auth mechanism. Email verification codes (for email change, not auth) are a separate flow covered under account recovery, not authentication.

Single IdP (Keycloak). User identity is bound to keycloak_id (UUID sub claim) + username. The get_current_wims_user function resolves users by keycloak_id first, then fallback to username. JIT provisioning creates new DB rows from token claims, preventing identity spoofing across IdPs.

JWT signature validated against JWKS with RS256. Signed assertions only - JWKS keys filtered by kty=RSA, use=sig, alg=RS256. Unverified or unsigned tokens rejected. Key rotation handled via kid matching + force-refresh fallback.

SAML not used in this stack (OIDC only). Authorization codes (OIDC) are uniquely processed and single-use per Keycloak default (accessCodeLifespan: 60s, single-use). Refresh token rotation... see V10.4.5 note on revokeRefreshToken: false.

OIDC ID Token claims validated: aud (audience = CLIENT_ID), iss (issuer = KEYCLOAK_ISSUER), exp, iat, sub. Token type discrimination via azp check (azp must equal CLIENT_ID). Nonce and state verified in frontend OIDC client (oidc.ts uses oidc-client-ts defaults).

Session management documentation: session token verification (auth.py), token refresh flow (auth-refresh.ts), OIDC configuration (oidc.ts), logout endpoints (context/AuthContext.tsx). Documented in system-wiki.
Session token type: Bearer JWT in HttpOnly cookie (not URL, not header). Self-contained JWT with RS256 signature. Token in __Host-access_token cookie. Refresh token in __Host-refresh_token cookie.

Session lifecycle defined: access token 5min, refresh token 24h cookie, SSO session 8h max/30min idle. Token rotation via /api/auth/refresh endpoint (POST). Revocation via Redis-backed SessionManager.
Session token verified on every request via get_current_user() dependency. JWT decoded with signature, audience, issuer, expiration validation against JWKS. No token caching - verified on each call.
Self-contained tokens (JWTs) used. Token contains all session data (sub, aud, exp, iat, iss, azp, realm_access, etc.). Backend validates locally against JWKS without DB lookup.
Session token uses ID token (JWT) - self-contained with user identity. Backend resolves to DB row via keycloak_id for authorization, but session validation is entirely JWT-based.
New session token issued on each authentication via Keycloak OIDC. Session tokens are not reused across authentication events. Each login creates new JWTs.
Inactivity timeout: ssoSessionIdleTimeout = 1800 (30 min). Session invalidated after inactivity period. Forced re-authentication required.
Absolute session timeout: ssoSessionMaxLifespan = 28800 (8 hours). Session terminated regardless of activity after 8 hours. Refresh token cookie has 24h maxAge but Keycloak SSO enforces 8h.

Session termination on logout: POST /api/auth/logout revokes refresh token, clears cookies, calls userManager.signoutRedirect to Keycloak end-session endpoint. Server-side session revocation via Keycloak admin API (user_logout).
Account disable terminates sessions: set_user_enabled(False) calls admin.user_logout() to force terminate all active sessions. Redis revocation timestamp set. Immediate effect.
Factor change terminates other sessions: email change requires re-authentication (current password + optional OTP). AuthContext logs user out and re-authenticates after email change flow.
Logout clearly visible in UI: user menu dropdown with 'Sign Out' option in Header component. Active session information displayed (username, role).
Admin session termination: POST /api/admin/users/{id}/logout via sessions.py. Uses admin kcadm API to force terminate sessions. get_system_admin guard required.
Email change requires re-authentication (current password + optional OTP). Password change via Keycloak requires current password. MFA re-enrollment handled by Keycloak.
Users can view own sessions via sessions.py endpoint (get_user_sessions). Admin can terminate sessions via admin endpoints. Self-service session termination requires re-authentication.

SSO session managed by Keycloak: ssoSessionIdleTimeout=1800s (30min), ssoSessionMaxLifespan=28800s (8h). IdP re-authentication required when SSO session expires. RP (WIMS backend) validates JWT expiration independently.
Session creation requires user authentication (Keycloak login page). No automatic or invisible session creation. User must explicitly authenticate with credentials.

evidence.source: src/backend/api/routes/ (48 imports of auth deps), system-wiki/security/security-baseline.md
evidence.finding: Authorization matrix documented in security-baseline.md. Per-route function-level guards (get_system_admin, get_national_validator, get_regional_encoder, get_analyst_or_admin, get_incident_viewer). Role hierarchy: SYSTEM_ADMIN > NATIONAL_ANALYST > NATIONAL_VALIDATOR > REGIONAL_ENCODER > CIVILIAN_REPORTER.

Field-level access control documentation not explicitly maintained. RLS policies provide row-level but field-level restrictions are implicit in the API schema (field-level Pydantic models per role visible). Risk: LOW.

evidence.source: src/backend/auth.py (get_system_admin, get_national_validator, get_regional_encoder, get_analyst_or_admin, get_incident_viewer, get_regional_user)
evidence.finding: Function-level access control enforced on every route. 48 route files import auth dependencies. Role-based guards raise 403 for unauthorized roles. Each guard checks current_user.role against allowed roles.

Data-specific access control via PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS). get_db_with_rls() sets RLS context via set_rls_context(). RLS policies in 10_rls_policies.sql enforce per-row tenant isolation based on user_id and assigned_region_id.

Field-level access restricted: different Pydantic schemas for different roles. Sensitive fields (e.g., incident_sensitive_details) encrypted via KMS with per-row crypto_provider. RLS policies restrict row visibility.
No client-side-only access control. All authorization checks happen server-side via FastAPI Depends. Role guards and RLS derive from JWT payload verified server-side, not from client-provided data.
Multi-tenant controls via PostgreSQL RLS. Tenant isolation by user_id + assigned_region_id. user_id (surrogate key) prevents cross-tenant access. RLS policies on all tenant-scoped tables.
JWT signature verified against JWKS from Keycloak. validate_token() checks signature using RSA public key from JWKS endpoint. Unsigned tokens rejected by jwt.decode().
Algorithm allowlist enforced: only RS256 accepted. JWKS keys filtered by kty=RSA, use=sig, alg=RS256. No 'none' algorithm allowed. Default signature algorithm in realm: RS256.
kid header validated against JWKS. Key selection by kid + fallback to all RSA signing keys if kid unknown. JWKS fetched from Keycloak with 60s cache TTL.
nbf and exp verified via jwt.decode options. require: ['exp', 'iat', 'iss', 'aud'] ensures expiration is enforced.
Token type discrimination: azp must equal CLIENT_ID. Access token vs ID token validation via claims. ID token nonce/state verified in oidc-client-ts frontend.
aud claim validated: jwt.decode(audience=AUDIENCE). CLIENT_ID and AUDIENCE configured via env vars, defaulting to 'wims-web'. iss validated against KEYCLOAK_ISSUER.
Instant revocation check via Redis: session_manager.is_token_revoked() compares iat against revocation timestamp. Revoked tokens rejected immediately.

OAuth as the only authentication service: Keycloak as authorization server. All flows use OAuth 2.0 / OIDC. Client credentials: wims-web (public client, authorization code flow), wims-admin-service (confidential client, direct access grant), bfp-client (public client, direct access grant for password verification).
OIDC client: oidc-client-ts library. Authorization code flow with PKCE. response_type='code' only. No token or id_token response_type exposed.
PKCE enforced: oidc-client-ts generates code_verifier and code_challenge (S256) automatically for all authorization code requests. wims-web client is public (no secret), making PKCE mandatory.

Redirect URI validation: oidc-client-ts validates redirect_uri against the configured exact value. Keycloak validates against the client's redirectUris allowlist. Exact matching prevents open redirect.

Resource server: backend acts as OAuth resource server. Token introspection via local JWT validation against JWKS (no per-request introspection endpoint call). RS256-signed tokens verified independently.
Resource server enforces authorization based on JWT claims: sub (user identity), realm_access.roles (WIMS role), azp (client). Scope validated via role hierarchy.
User identity from iss + sub combination. keycloak_id (UUID from JWT sub) is unique per IdP and not reassignable. Username fallback with drift detection prevents identity collision.

Auth strength implicitly verified: only RS256-signed tokens accepted via JWKS. Token expiration (exp) verified. No explicit acr/amr/auth_time validation but Keycloak is the sole IdP with consistent authentication strength.

Authorization code redirect URI allowlist: wims-web client has explicit allowlist (https://localhost/callback, http://localhost/callback, https://wimsbfp.tech/callback, https://wims.bfp.gov.ph/*, etc.). Wildcards at path level only. No open redirect.
Authorization code single-use: Keycloak invalidates auth code after first use. accessCodeLifespan: 60 seconds. Repeated calls with same code return error.

Authorization code short-lived: accessCodeLifespan = 60 seconds (under 10-min L2 limit). accessCodeLifespanLogin = 1800 (30 min), accessCodeLifespanUserAction = 300 (5 min). Auth code is the primary short code.

PKCE challenge methods: S256 enforced by oidc-client-ts. However, the backends auth code exchange (server-side) behavior when receiving 'plain' challenge not explicitly tested. Keycloak accepts 'plain' by default. Risk: LOW due to oidc-client-ts emitting S256.

Refresh token rotation NOT enforced. revokeRefreshToken: false means old refresh tokens remain valid after use. refreshTokenMaxReuse: 0 is irrelevant when rotation is disabled. This is a known gap: the frontend auth-refresh.ts uses Web Locks API to prevent race conditions but cannot provide rotation. Risk: HIGH - stolen refresh token can be reused indefinitely. Remediation: Set revokeRefreshToken: true in Keycloak realm config.
Authentication code replay: Keycloak rejects replayed auth codes (single-use + 60s expiry). State parameter validated via oidc-client-ts (nonce + state in authorization request).
Nonce and state: oidc-client-ts generates and validates nonce and state parameters. State bound to browser session. Nonce prevents CSRF on the auth code flow.
Authorization server uses openid scope. Backend validates JWT aud and azp claims to prevent token replay across clients.
State parameter: oidc-client-ts generates a random state value for each authorization request and validates it on callback. Prevents CSRF on OAuth callback.
Confidential client authentication: wims-admin-service uses client-secret authenticator with service account. Keycloak supports client_secret_basic and client_secret_post. Secret stored in env var.
Public client authentication: wims-web (public), bfp-client (public), admin-cli (public). No client_secret for public clients - PKCE + redirect URI validation provide security.

evidence.source: src/frontend/src/lib/oidc.ts (OpenID Connect scope: openid profile email)
evidence.finding: OpenID Connect: scope includes 'openid profile email'. ID Token issued alongside access token. nonce and state verified by oidc-client-ts. Backend validates sub, aud, iss, exp.
ID Token audience validation: aud claim validated against AUDIENCE (defaults to wims-web client ID). Token rejected if aud does not match.
Pass-through of authentication assertions: realm_access.roles parsed for WIMS roles. Backend does not modify or create roles - trusts Keycloak for role assignment.
OIDC ID Token with azp check: azp claim validated against CLIENT_ID. Backend verifies the token was issued to the correct client.
WIMS-BFP does not use OIDC back-channel logout. Logout is front-channel (signoutRedirect) with Keycloak end-session endpoint.
Registration: registrationAllowed: false. Self-registration disabled. User creation only via admin API (create_keycloak_user). Prevents unauthorized account creation.
User deprovisioning: set_user_enabled(False) disables account and revokes sessions. Admin API for user deletion available. No automatic deprovisioning - requires admin action.
Keycloak consent enabled for OIDC clients. User prompted for consent on first authorization. Client identity assured via redirect URI allowlist + PKCE.
Keycloak displays consent screen with scopes requested (openid, profile, email) and client identity (wims-web). User can review what information is shared.
Users can review, modify, and revoke granted consents via Keycloak account console (/realms/bfp/account). Admin can also manage via kcadm.
Key management policy documented in security-baseline.md S_OpenBao KMSS. OpenBao runbook covers key lifecycle, rotation, and access control. Master key stored in OpenBao, not in source code.

Crypto inventory documented: AES-256-GCM (via SecurityProvider and KmsSecurityProvider), Argon2id/PBKDF2 (Keycloak password hashing), SHA-256 for hashing. Algorithm locations: backend/services/kms/, utils/crypto.py.

Industry-validated algorithms: AES-256-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D), Argon2id (OWASP recommended), PBKDF2 (NIST SP 800-132). No custom crypto implementations. OpenBao Transit provides FIPS 140-2 validated HSM-backed encryption.

Crypto agility via provider dispatch pattern. crypto_provider column on wims.incident_sensitive_details allows hot-swapping between SecurityProvider (env var key) and KmsSecurityProvider (OpenBao Transit). New algorithms can be added by implementing the provider interface.
128-bit security minimum satisfied by AES-256 (256-bit key, 128-bit security level). Minimum key size: 256 bits (AES-256). OpenBao Transit uses 256-bit keys by default.
AES-256-GCM in use. GCM provides authenticated encryption (confidentiality + integrity). No ECB mode used. No CTR mode without MAC.
No non-IO, non-security-relevant modes (ECB, CBC without MAC) in use. GCM provides built-in integrity verification via authentication tag.
GCM mode provides authenticated encryption (confidentiality + integrity via authentication tag). No separate MAC required. GCM is NIST SP 800-38D approved AEAD mode.

evidence.source: rg -w MD5|sha1|SHA1 src/ --type py returns 0 hits
evidence.finding: No MD5, SHA-1, or other deprecated hash functions in use. SHA-256 for hashing. PBKDF2 for password hashing (Keycloak). SHA-256 in JWT RS256 signatures.

evidence.source: Keycloak password hashing (PBKDF2 with work factor)
evidence.finding: Keycloak uses PBKDF2 (or Argon2id in newer versions) for password storage. Password hashing meets ASVS requirements. Work factor configurable via Keycloak.
CSPRNG sources: secrets.randbelow (auth.py), secrets.choice (keycloak_admin.py), os.urandom (Python standard library). No random module used for security-sensitive operations.
KDF used for secret derivation: OpenBao Transit derive key functionality. PBKDF2 for password hashing (Keycloak). Encryption keys derived securely.
CSPRNG used for all randomness: secrets.randbelow (6-digit codes, 10^6 = ~20 bits), secrets.choice (14-char temp passwords = ~87 bits). OpenBao Transit provides CSPRNG for encryption operations.
Public key crypto: RS256 (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256). Key management via Keycloak JWKS. Minimum key size: 2048-bit RSA. OpenBao Transit for symmetric encryption only.
TLS 1.3 only in production HTTPS block. Server: nginx, protocol: TLSv1.3. No earlier TLS versions enabled. dev HTTP block is localhost-only.

Strong cipher suites only: ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305, ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305. TLS 1.3 ciphersuites: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256. No weak ciphers.
HTTPS enforced for production: HTTP->HTTPS redirect server block for wimsbfp.tech. HSTS header: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains.
Frontend always served over HTTPS in production via nginx TLS termination. HSTS ensures browser always uses HTTPS.
HSTS header: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. Preload not configured but optional.

evidence.source: Docker Compose env, PostgreSQL connection string
evidence.finding: Backend-to-PostgreSQL uses ?sslmode=disable for Docker bridge network (local dev). Production TLS configuration for inter-service communication not verified. Assessment: dev stack uses Docker bridge, sslmode=disable; production TBD.
No verify=False found in Python code (rg verify=False returns 0 hits). Keycloak OIDC client uses verify=True. Certificate validation enforced for all outbound TLS connections.
Same as V12.3.1: inter-service TLS not verified. Backend->PostgreSQL uses sslmode=disable in Docker bridge. Production TLS between services TBD.
No certificate pinning (HPKP or similar) implemented. nginx uses Let's Encrypt certificates. Remediation: monitor certificate changes; pinning not recommended for typical deployments.

Communication needs documented in security-baseline.md: Suricata network monitoring (tier 6), Keycloak OIDC (auth), Postgres/Redis (data layer), OpenBao (secrets), Ollama (XAI), MailHog (dev email), Nominatim (geocode). FRS Module 1 (Architecture) and Module 13 (Notifications) cover the design. See 'Backend Communication' tier table for the full component map.

Backend components use appropriate auth: Postgres via wims_app_user (DB session), Redis via its protocol, Keycloak via OIDC client credentials, OpenBao via service token, Ollama via HTTP (no auth — dev only). Each component has a distinct auth mechanism appropriate to its protocol. The application does not share user session tokens with backend services.

Service accounts are used: wims_app_user (limited DB grants via RLS, scoped to wims schema), svc_suricata system account (auto-created for Suricata incident auto-creation), svc_task (KMS rotation). Keycloak admin client credentials are used for JIT user provisioning, not for end-user auth. The system does not use root/admin for application-level operations.

No default credentials in use: POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required (compose :?error), KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD is required, WIMS_MASTER_KEY is required for env_aesgcm crypto. Service accounts (svc_suricata, svc_task) use generated UUIDs not default names. Redis has no password in dev compose — acceptable for prototype but would need a password in production.

ExternalServiceClient.__init__ builds allowlist from OLLAMA_URL+OPENBAO_ADDR+NOMINATIM_URL+EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ALLOWED_HOSTS+docker hostnames. request_async/request_sync check hostname before circuit breaker (no DNS resolution). Rejects with ExternalServiceError. TDD: 3 new tests, RED->GREEN. Allowlist logged at INFO at init.

Nginx is a reverse proxy — it doesn't initiate outbound requests itself. The backend's outbound HTTP goes through utils/external_service.py (no allowlist — see V13.2.4). For a defense-in-depth posture, the application should restrict outbound destinations to known services (Ollama, OpenBao, Nominatim, Keycloak). Currently the backend can call any URL that resolves.

v5.0.0-V13.2.5.remediation: Same remediation as V13.2.4 — implement allowlist at the application layer. Nginx outbound restrictions would require a forward proxy, which is out of scope for the prototype.

evidence.finding: Secrets management uses two layers: (1) env_aesgcm — AES-256-GCM with WIMS_MASTER_KEY from env (default for prototype), (2) OpenBao Transit engine for key rotation in production-like deployments (tasks/kms_rotation.py handles rotation). WIMS_CRYPTO_PROVIDER env var selects the provider. api/routes/incidents.py:443 reads the provider at runtime. Database encryption, file encryption, and KMS are all routed through this abstraction.

Access to secrets follows least privilege: wims_app_user has schema-scoped grants (RLS-enforced, row-level policies per table). svc_suricata is a system account with INSERT-only on fire_incidents (auto-creation). svc_task has SELECT/UPDATE on kms_key_rotation_runs. RLS policies (`security_logs_admin_only`, `audit_trails_insert_service`) restrict per-role. No single role has access to all secrets.

Backend Dockerfile uses `COPY . .` which would copy the .git directory UNLESS excluded. .dockerignore explicitly lists `.git` (along with .venv, __pycache__, tests, storage, AFOR-FORMATTED.xlsx) — confirmed present. The deployed image does NOT contain .git metadata. Nginx also does not serve .git paths (no .git location block in nginx config).

No debug mode enabled: Dockerfile CMD is `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 3 --limit-concurrency 200 --timeout-keep-alive 5` — no `--reload` flag. No `debug=True` in main.py. No DEBUG/RELOAD env vars in .env or docker-compose.yml. FastAPI's debug mode would also need to be explicitly enabled via `app.debug = True` (not present).

No directory listings: grep for `autoindex` across all nginx configs returns no matches. Nginx default is `autoindex off`; the configs do not override it. FastAPI also does not serve directory listings (it only serves registered routes). Static file serving in nginx (if any) is restricted to specific paths.

Suricata SID 1000129 DETECTS TRACE in IDS alert mode (does not block — 0 drop/reject rules across 48,693 active ET + 50 custom rules). nginx has no explicit TRACE block (only CORS Access-Control-Allow-Methods response header). FastAPI/uvicorn 405 default for unregistered methods plausibly rejects TRACE, but not runtime-verified. Recommend: curl -X TRACE https://wimsbfp.tech/ and confirm 405/403.

All admin/monitoring endpoints use `Depends(get_system_admin)` dependency injection: api/routes/admin/scheduled_reports.py, analytics.py, security.py all guard every route. /api/admin/monitoring/* (system, workers, security-logs) is restricted to SYSTEM_ADMIN role. The monitoring page is not externally accessible without admin auth. Suricata's eve.json is the only IDS-specific endpoint exposed and goes through the same admin gating.

Sensitive data is classified. The PII encryption spec (2026-06-23) defines protection levels for witness narrative, caller name, contact info, location. The OpenBao KMS runbook documents the encryption tiers (env_aesgcm for at-rest, OpenBao Transit for production). FRS Module 6 (Compliance & Data Privacy) and Module 15 (Reference Data) define the data taxonomy.

Protection requirements are documented per level: encryption (AES-256-GCM via WIMS_MASTER_KEY or OpenBao Transit), integrity verification (PostgreSQL constraints + RLS), retention (incident lifecycle), logging (audit trail), access controls (RLS per role). Security-baseline.md tier table references all controls.

evidence.source: src/backend/api/routes/* (full grep for api_key, session_token, password in query strings)
evidence.finding: No routes pass sensitive data in URL or query string. Grep for `api_key`, `session_token`, `password` in query parameters returns no matches. Sensitive data flows through request body (JSON) or Authorization headers (OIDC). The XAI prompt does embed raw_payload which can contain credentials — see V16.2.5 NOT-VERIFIED for that specific path.

Sensitive data responses carry Cache-Control: no-store. /api/admin/privacy/export returns headers `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`. /api/events/stream (SSE) returns `Cache-Control: no-cache` to prevent buffering. Test `test_privacy.py:212` asserts no-store on export responses. Nginx does not add its own cache headers that would override these.

No third-party trackers or analytics services. The frontend does not include Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, Mixpanel, Segment, or similar. OpenBao, Ollama, Keycloak, Postgres, Redis, Nominatim are all self-hosted. The /api/events/stream SSE channel stays within the same origin. No external beacons.

Daily 03:00 UTC Celery task. Per-table strategies: soft-archive VERIFIED fire_incidents (is_archived=TRUE), hard-delete non-VERIFIED, REAL blob-erasure (NULL all PII + pii_blob_enc + encryption_iv + data_retention_erased_at=now) for incident_sensitive_details, no-op for IVH+audit_trails. Config-driven via system_config (6 retention.*_days keys seeded). Audit logged. TDD: 5 new tests, RED->GREEN. Migration 68 applied.

On logout, `localStorage.removeItem(SESSION_CACHE_KEY)` is called (line 236). The session cache (`wims:offline_session_cache`) contains `{ user: data.user }` from the last successful login. After logout, the cache is cleared. No `Clear-Site-Data` HTTP header is set, but the localStorage clear handles the most common case. **No `Clear-Site-Data` header is a minor finding** (the header would also clear cookies, cache, storage — not just localStorage).

Anti-caching headers are set on sensitive responses: /api/admin/privacy/export uses `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`; /api/events/stream (SSE) uses `Cache-Control: no-cache`. The frontend does not cache authenticated responses (Next.js with `cache: 'no-store'` on fetch options where sensitive). Nginx does not add ETag/Last-Modified that would override.

localStorage.setItem now stores only {id, role} (was full user with email/name/preferred_username). Pick<User,id|role> type. serverValidated=false on offline restore. TDD: 3 new tests, RED->GREEN. Frontend lint clean (0 errors).
Software supply chain security: pip-audit in CI pipeline (requirements.txt). Docker images pinned (Python 3.10-slim). No breached components detected in current scan.
SBOM available via requirements.txt + package-lock.json. Dependency scanning via pip-audit and npm audit in CI pipeline.
HTTP request body size limits enforced at nginx (50 MB) and FastAPI default limits.
No components with breached remediation time identified. pip-audit run in CI. Dependencies maintained.
Rate limiting for slow operations: nginx limit_req + backend Redis rate limiter. Async processing for long-running tasks via Celery.
No documented evidence that the security of the supply chain is verified. pip-audit runs in CI but no formal supply chain security review process documented.
Compartmentalization between user groups via role-based routing and API guards. Role-specific layouts and page access in frontend (dashboard/regional, dashboard/validator, dashboard/analyst, admin).
RLS policies enforce per-row tenant isolation. User sessions isolated by Redis session_manager with per-user revocation. Cross-tenant data access prevented.
Mass assignment protection via Pydantic BaseModel. extra='forbid' config ensures unknown fields are rejected. No direct assignment from request body to database models.
Real IP forwarding: X-Real-IP set to $realip_remote_addr (TCP socket). X-Forwarded-For uses $realip_remote_addr for rate limiting. Trusted proxy range: 172.18.0.0/16 + 127.0.0.1.
Type-safe comparisons used in critical paths. Python type hints + Pydantic validation ensure type safety. is operator for None checks, not ==.
Frontend uses modern JS (Set/Map). No object literal for hash maps. TypeScript strict mode.
HTTP parameter pollution not exploitable. FastAPI does not merge query, body, and cookie parameters. Each endpoint explicitly specifies its parameter source (Query, Body, Cookie).

IDS/XAI section documents all logging layers: Suricata eve.json → wims.security_threat_logs → Celery beat ingest → Ollama XAI → xai_narrative. Tier-6 'IDS/XAI' subsection enumerates pipeline stages with file paths and line numbers.

security_threat_logs has: log_id, timestamp (when), source_ip/destination_ip (where), suricata_sid/severity_level/raw_payload (what), xai_narrative (AI analysis). 'Who' is N/A for network IDS (no end-user attribution in Suricata flow).
All security tables use TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now() — PostgreSQL returns UTC timestamp with timezone offset. system_audit_trails.timestamp and security_threat_logs.timestamp are both timestamptz.

Python logging uses default stdout/stderr (docker logs captures). No log_file/syslog/graylog/datadog references in code. Suricata eve.json is the only file-based log. Both destinations documented in security-baseline.md.

Suricata emits NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) — a standard, structured format. Backend parses via parse_eve_alert_line() and stores in structured columns. Cross-correlation via log_id. Python app logs are plain text but not security-critical.

analyze_threat_log() interpolates raw_payload (attacker-controlled network data) directly into the Ollama prompt with f-string. No redaction layer. Network payloads can contain credentials in plaintext (HTTP Basic Auth, form POSTs, cookies). The XAI prompt is an outbound log channel to an external LLM. **Potential sensitive data exposure** — needs runtime audit of which raw_payloads are sent.

v5.0.0-V16.2.5.remediation: Add a payload-redaction layer in analyze_threat_log() that strips/masks: HTTP Authorization headers, cookies, form-encoded credentials, JWT tokens, email addresses (PII). Document the redaction policy in security-baseline.md.

evidence.finding: LOGIN action_type is logged with user_id, ip_address, user_agent, timestamp, correlation_id, result (success/failure). 48 LOGIN events in dev seed data. system_audit_trails has a `result` column that explicitly tracks success/failure.

Authorization failures are logged as action_types. VERIFY_REJECT (validator rejected incident), CITIZEN_REPORT_REJECTED_INSUFFICIENT (insufficient data = rejected), and INTEGRITY_VIOLATION are all authorization-decision events. result column tracks success/failure per event.

Suricata alerts feed security_threat_logs via 10s Celery beat (ingest_suricata_eve). Custom WIMS SIDs 1000001-1000134 cover SQLi/XSS/SSRF/TRACE/etc — security control bypass attempts are detected and logged. Previously audited 2026-06-23.

Uvicorn logs unhandled exceptions to stderr with full stack trace by default. Python logging.getLogger('wims.*') writes to stdout. main.py has 4 @app.middleware('http') handlers that log request paths/errors. All exceptions reach the logger before the 500 response is sent.

raw_payload and severity_level wrapped in json.dumps() in analyze_threat_log() prompt to prevent delimiter-breakout log injection. TDD: test_analyze_threat_log_escapes_raw_payload (RED->GREEN). Scope: XAI prompt only; other logger call sites deferred (hygiene, not remotely exploitable).

security_threat_logs has RLS: POLICY 'security_logs_admin_only' USING (wims.current_user_role() = ANY (ARRAY['SYSTEM_ADMIN','NATIONAL_ANALYST'])). system_audit_trails has 'audit_trails_insert_service' for INSERT. No UPDATE/DELETE policies = append-only. Both tables have forced RLS enabled.

evidence.source: single-VPS prototype architecture (documented in docs/agents/ci-preflight.md + AGENTS.md)
evidence.finding: WIMS-BFP is a single-VPS prototype. No separate logging system (syslog server, SIEM, cloud log service) is in scope. Logs stay on the same host as the application. This is a known/accepted architectural constraint for the prototype phase. Would be COMPLIANT in production with a separate SIEM/log shipper.

@app.exception_handler(Exception) returns generic 500 for unhandled exceptions. HTTPException handler NOT overridden (4xx keep messages). 7 real 5xx leakers cleaned in sessions.py + admin/backups.py: f-string str(e) replaced with generic messages, errors logged server-side. TDD: 2 new tests, RED->GREEN.

Redis rate-limit middleware fails open (documented choice, logged as warning). Ollama calls return 502 on ConnectError/TimeoutException (graceful). Suricata ingest has its own try/except (ingest_eve_file). The system continues to operate when external resources fail, with appropriate logging.

rate_limit_middleware now fail-closed on Redis down (returns 503 + Retry-After:30 on /api/auth/callback POST). Dev escape hatch via RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_OPEN env var. TDD: 3 new tests, RED->GREEN. blocked_ip_middleware fail-open deliberately preserved (documented asymmetry).
No TURN/STUN server, no media streaming, no WebRTC signaling in the WIMS-BFP stack.
No TURN server configured.
No TURN server configured.
No TURN server configured.
No TURN server configured. WebRTC not used.
No media security concerns - no audio/video streaming.
No media security concerns.
No WebRTC implementation in frontend or backend.
Upload size limit: client_max_body_size 50M in nginx. File type restrictions: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .pdf, .doc, .docx allowed (src/backend/utils/upload_validation.py). User limits also enforced.
No document-based virus/malware scanning implemented. Upload validation covers extension + magic bytes but not AV scanning. Risk: LOW for prototype but should be addressed for production.
Files stored with restricted permissions. Docker volume not served by nginx. No direct URL access to uploaded files.
Content-Type validation on responses. FastAPI defaults enforce application/json for JSON responses. ORJSON encoder used. Content-Type headers not client-overridable.
HTTP request body size limits enforced via nginx client_max_body_size 50M + FastAPI default request size limits. Request smuggling prevented by FastAPI/Starlette HTTP parser.
HTTP method override headers not supported. FastAPI does not accept X-HTTP-Method-Override or similar headers by default.
HTTP/1.1 only (no HTTP/2 enabled). Version consistency not a concern. Suricata rules (SID 1000129) block TRACE/CONNECT methods.

No strict Content-Type header validation on backend endpoints. FastAPI reads Content-Type from request but does not enforce application/json for all POST endpoints. Non-JSON content types may be accepted where JSON is expected. Risk: MED. Remediation: Add middleware rejecting non-JSON Content-Type on JSON-only endpoints.

Input validation duplicated at trusted service (backend). Even though frontend validates, backend re-validates all input via Pydantic models. Defense in depth: frontend validation is UX-only; backend validation is security-critical.
Anti-automation for unauthenticated civilian report submission. Rate limiting + CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA on public DMZ endpoints.
No documented data processing policy for personal data explicitly documented. PII handling is implicit in the security-baseline.md. Risk: LOW for prototype.
No dangerous functionality exposed. Debug endpoints disabled via env var gating. Server-tokens: off in nginx. HTTP methods restricted per endpoint.

Concurrency-safe atomic operations not fully verified. SQLAlchemy session handling via get_db_with_rls includes proper commit/rollback. Celery tasks for async processing. Redis atomic operations for rate limiting. Risk: LOW for typical CRUD workload.
Embedded or environment-based configuration. Config management pattern not fully documented. Remediation: document config loading precedence and validation.
No formal crypto agility process document. The provider dispatch pattern enables algorithm swapping but no documented process for deprecation/transition. Risk: LOW for prototype.

HSTS header: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. TLS enforced for production (HTTP->HTTPS redirect). Cookie security: Set-Cookie uses Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; __Host- prefix (auth-refresh route).
User-agent origin authentication: OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE. Callback redirectUri validated via oidc-client-ts. nonce and state verified.

No periodic re-authentication for high-value functions. Admin operations are gated by role but do not require re-authentication after initial login. Risk: LOW for prototype, MED for production with sensitive admin operations.

Token endpoint authentication: public clients use PKCE instead of client_secret. wims-web has no secret (publicClient: true). bfp-client and admin-cli also public. wims-admin-service uses client_secret_basic via service account.
Client credentials: wims-admin-service stores secret in env var (KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET). No hardcoded secrets. Production secret management via .env file or OpenBao.
Access token validation: JWT signature verified against JWKS. audience (aud) validated. issuer (iss) validated. azp (authorized party) validated against CLIENT_ID. Expiration enforced.
Access token replay prevention: token tied to specific client via azp check. Revocation via Redis timestamp check. Short-lived (5-min) tokens limit replay window.
Token issuer validation: iss claim validated against KEYCLOAK_ISSUER env var. Prevents token injection from arbitrary issuers.
Authorization from token claims: role resolved from JWT realm_access.roles and resource_access. WIMS_ROLES_FROM_KEYCLOAK hierarchy enforced server-side.

Backend service uses service account (wims-admin-service) for admin operations. Client credentials flow for server-to-server communication. Least privilege: service account scoped to admin operations only.

Administrative functions: admin routes protected by get_system_admin guard. User management, role assignment, session management via admin API. All administrative actions logged in system_audit_trails.
